messages:
maria: Customer on Dedicated (us-east) reporting sudden latency spikes + intermittent 502s right after a canary flip to redwood-v2.2. Need repro artifacts: request IDs, curl reproducer, debug bundle, and confirm if we should pin back to v2.1.

jun: Can you paste a sample request_id and approximate time window? Also which route/model name did they hit?

maria: req: rq_7a9b3f2d, approx 2026-03-12T14:02:31Z. Route: POST /v1/generate model=redwood-v2.2-canary. They also saw streaming truncation on the client.

alex: Flagging SRE to look for proxy retries and 502 origins. @sam can you pull ingress/nginx logs for that req id?

sam: On it. Also ask customer to run a simple non-streaming curl so we can capture full HTTP exchange. Example to send them:

curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: rq_7a9b3f2d" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v2.2-canary","input":"short prompt to trigger"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

They should include the full -v output and response headers. If they use streaming, have them add --no-buffer and --max-time 30.

maria: Customer shared a streaming curl that timed out. I asked them to re-run with --max-time 30 and to include header X-Client-Trace: trace_4f1b so we can map traces.

ops-bot: Deploy bot: canary swap completed 2026-03-12T13:58:00Z -> models/redwood-v2.2-canary promoted in us-east. Rollback available.

jun: If this looks like a regression from v2.1 -> v2.2 we should pin the customer back to v2.1 while we debug. Maria, did they request immediate pin? Also we need their debug bundle from the Dedicated host: fetch /_debug/bundle and upload to the ticket.

maria: They want to be pinned back for now. Asked them to upload debug bundle + gateway logs. Upload endpoint: https://uploads.redwood.ai/support/attachments (they will paste object id once uploaded).

sam: For a complete repro set collect: 1) curl -v output (full), 2) X-Request-ID, 3) gateway/nginx logs for the time window, 4) infer/runtime logs on the GPU node (infer.log), 5) the prompt/seed used, and 6) response headers (look for X-Fallback-Model, X-Route, X-Server-Retry). If fallback triggered, we need which variant served the request.

alex: Note: admin API to pin a customer back (example):

POST /admin/customers/{id}/pin
{ "model": "redwood-v2.1-stable", "reason": "customer regression" }

This will route them to the stable model until we clear it.

maria: Customer uploaded debug bundle id: dbg_0037 and attached curl output. They ran the reproducer twice: first returned 502, second succeeded but had ~300ms tail latency and response header X-Fallback-Model: redwood-v2.1-stable.

jun: Hmm — looks like the router attempted fallback when v2.2 returned an error. Need to verify fallback policy and canary capacity during 13:58-14:05. @sam pull canary host logs & kernel selection traces.

sam: Downloading logs now. Requesting runtime to dump kvcache metrics and kernel-selection traces for the canary instances in that window. May take a few minutes.

maria: I pinned the customer back to redwood-v2.1-stable and confirmed with them. Monitoring for errors. If 502s continue after pin, we escalate to infra.

alex: When this is resolved we need a short postmortem: timeline, root cause (model code vs infra), whether fallback behaved correctly, and any changes to rollout/fallback settings. For now, disable canary routing for this customer.

maria: Thanks — I'll keep the ticket updated and schedule a follow-up at 16:00 UTC to review logs and decide on re-rollout.

sam: Got the logs; first pass shows a spike in kernel launch time on the canary hosts coincident with the first failures. Sharing artifacts in the ticket (logs + trace ids).

maria: Great. Customer appreciates quick action. I'll close the loop after the 16:00 review. :thumbsup:
